_README: Where every picture lives, and what it is called. WRITTEN BY HAND.
Drop a PNG into the right folder under the right name and it appears in
the game - no code, no re-export. Anything not drawn yet shows as a
coloured placeholder labelled with the file it is waiting for.
CHARACTERS: {ID}_{expression}.png in the folder for their kind.
protagonists  PC01-PC04          player.json
opponents     OP01...            opponents.json
staff         SF01...            staff.json
visitors      VI01...            visitors.json
journalists   JR_A...            journalists.json
e.g. assets/characters/opponents/OP03_attacking.png
EXPRESSIONS: the five every character should have, in the order to draw
them. neutral first - it is what every other face falls back to.
neutral    at rest, listening
attacking  about to go for you (their intent is an attack)
guarding   bracing, arms folded (their intent is to block)
gaining    rallying their side (their intent is to gain support)
damaged    just hit, or losing the room
Two optional extras: defeated (argued down) and victory (protagonist,
on winning). A face that is missing uses expression_fallbacks, and in
the end neutral, so a character with only a neutral drawing works.
STAGE OUTFITS (entirely optional): {ID}_{STAGE_ID}_{expression}.png,
e.g. OP03_ST04_attacking.png for how OP03 looks only in a press
conference. Tried before the plain file of that expression; nothing has
to be drawn for this, and it is not counted by the art checklist - only
draw one where a character genuinely dresses or poses differently in
one room.
EVERYTHING ELSE: {ID}.png
cards        card art by card ID, e.g. C11.png (the picture in the
card's window, not the frame)
backgrounds  by stage ID, e.g. ST02.png, plus OFFICE.png
icons        organisations (BO04.png), items (the Shop tab's Icon
name), suits, meta-variables
SIZES (portrait canvas is 1080 x 2340): characters 1024 x 1280
(4:5, figure from the waist up, transparent background); card art
1024 x 768; backgrounds 1080 x 2340; icons 256 x 256.
legacy_folders: where art was looked for before this scheme. Still
checked last, so nothing already drawn goes missing. Move files into the
new folders when convenient.
tools/art_checklist.py writes design/ART_CHECKLIST.md: every file the
data asks for, and which are drawn.
